correctness.rationale: For every step the exact identity d(y,F(x))=bar d(pi y,T pi x) holds. Arbitrary quotient orbit lifts are genuine F orbits, and nearest-fibre lifts preserve shadowing errors. Taking a least common multiple of pseudo-orbit and tracing-orbit periods yields a periodic F lift. The same identity yields F^n(x)=pi^{-1}(T^n pi x) and the weighted point counts. The positive-expansivity implications are proved from nearest lifts and the uniform separation of distinct free-group orbit members. In the nonfree two-sheet shift wedge, arbitrarily close distinct twin points have intersecting images and hence coalescing F orbits. The full-shift fixed-point census gives 2^{n+1}-1 and formal zeta (1-z)/(1-2z)^2. None of these steps relies on finite experiments.

Targeted statement-level published-research searches and accessible prior-claim comparisons did not yield an equivalent theorem or stronger covering result. value.rationale: Finite-symmetry constructions are a natural systematic class of set-valued dynamics. The result gives a complete reduction of both orbit-tracing properties at unchanged tolerances, a precise fibre-weighted periodic-return invariant, and an exact boundary at which positive expansivity fails despite an expansive full-shift quotient. The explicit branched example shows why a freeness hypothesis matters in applying expansivity-based theorems; this structural failure would not follow merely from computing a special case or renaming a definition.
